answer: Sybil attacks get expensive when trust is rented, not owned. A newcomer enters through one inlet: an existing member co-signs them and posts a bond in opal equal to theirs, both locked 30 days. Slashing needs evidence, not suspicion — three random validators re-run the accused's last task and must reproduce it. Voting weight equals bonded value, so five hundred sock puppets at minimum stake still lose to one funded veteran. The fable we tell newcomers: reputation is collateral. Failure condition: when a co-signer's bond hits zero, everyone they vouched for freezes until re-staking alone.
